note: No absolute or relative logic-density figure for 28nm found in TSMC publications (the 28nm volume-production release gives none). Chain link to the next node: TSMC states 16FinFET has 'twice the gate density of TSMC's 28HPM process' (pr.tsmc.com/english/news/1826, 2014-09-25).

Relative only (TSMC): 16FinFET 'has twice the gate density of TSMC's 28HPM process' (pr.tsmc.com/english/news/1826, 2014-09-25; stated for 16FinFET, the predecessor of 16FF+); 16FF+ 'operates 40% faster than ... 20SoC' or 'consumes 50% less power at the same speed' (pr.tsmc.com/english/news/1835) - no 16FF+ density figure. 16FFC in volume production since Q1 2016 (2015 Annual Report). TSMC 10nm: '2.1X gate density improvement over 16nm' (2015 Annual Report). No absolute MTr/mm2 published by TSMC.

No numeric density figure: 2018 Annual Report says only that 12FFC 'drives die size and power consumption to the best levels of the foundry's 16/14nm technologies'. The '12 nm FFN' used for NVIDIA V100 is a customer-specific variant; TSMC publishes no data on FFN, so map it to this row only with that caveat.

Relative only (TSMC): N7 offers '3 times logic density improvement over 16nm (N16)' (tsmc.com mobile platform page; HPC platform page says '3 times the logic density, compared to 16nm (N16)'; 2018 Annual Report 'more than three times the logic density'). No absolute MTr/mm2 published by TSMC. N7+ (EUV) was 'first EUV process to enter volume production' (HPC page), no density figure recorded.
Relative only (TSMC): 'TSMC's N6 process delivers 18% higher logic density over the N7 process.' (pr.tsmc.com/english/news/1989, 2019-04-16). No absolute MTr/mm2 published by TSMC.

Relative only (TSMC): 'N5 provides a 15% performance gain or a 30% power reduction, and up to 80% logic density gain over the preceding N7 technology.' (pr.tsmc.com/english/news/2729, 2020-08-25). No absolute MTr/mm2 published by TSMC. N5P: volume production 2021 (2022 Annual Report: second year in 2022).

No numeric density figure: TSMC says only that N4 'features density improvement' over N5 (mobile platform page) and 'further improves performance, power efficiency and transistor density' (pr.tsmc.com/english/news/2831). N4P volume production 2023 (mobile page). NVIDIA's '4N'/'4NP' are customer-specific variants on which TSMC publishes nothing; map H100/B200 to this row only with that caveat.

Relative only (TSMC): N3 offers 'a logic density gain up to 70% over N5' (pr.tsmc.com/english/news/2729, 2020-08-25); 2021 release: N3 will 'provide up to 70% logic density gain' vs N5 (pr.tsmc.com/english/news/2831). Original N3 (sometimes called N3B). No absolute MTr/mm2 published by TSMC.

Relative only (TSMC): N3E gives 'approximately 1.6 times logic density increase compared to N5 technology' (tsmc.com mobile platform page) - lower than N3's 1.7x. No absolute MTr/mm2 published by TSMC.

Relative only (TSMC): N3P 'offers an additional boost to N3E with 5% more speed at the same leakage' ... 'and 1.04X more chip density' (pr.tsmc.com/english/news/3021, 2023-04-26; chip density = mixed logic/SRAM/analog, not logic density). No absolute MTr/mm2 published by TSMC.

Relative only (TSMC): N2 'greater than 1.15X chip density' vs N3E (pr.tsmc.com/english/news/3021, 2023-04-26, alongside 'up to 15% speed improvement over N3E at the same power'); N2P '1.2 times logic density, and 1.15 times chip density over N3E' (tsmc.com HPC platform page). Later: A16 'up to 1.10 times chip density' vs N2P; A14 'more than a 20% increase in logic density' vs N2 (HPC page). No absolute MTr/mm2 published by TSMC.

No density figure: vs 20nm the release states 'up to 20 percent faster speed, 35 percent less power consumption and 30 percent productivity gain' (productivity, not density). No absolute MTr/mm2 published by Samsung.

Relative only (Samsung): 10LPE allows 'up to 30-percent increase in area efficiency' vs its 14nm predecessor (same release). 'Area efficiency' is not defined (could be read as area reduction or density gain); do not convert. No absolute MTr/mm2 published by Samsung.

Relative only (Samsung): 7LPP 'delivers up to a 40% increase in area efficiency with 20% higher performance or up to 50% lower power consumption' vs its 10nm FinFET predecessors (2018-10-18 release). No absolute MTr/mm2 published by Samsung.

Relative only (Samsung): 'Compared to 7nm, Samsung's 5nm FinFET process technology provides up to a 25 percent increase in logic area efficiency with 20 percent lower power consumption or 10 percent higher performance' (news.samsung.com, 2019-04-16). No absolute MTr/mm2 published by Samsung.

Relative only (Samsung): 'Compared to 5nm process, the first-generation 3nm process can reduce power consumption by up to 45%, improve performance by 23% and reduce area by 16% compared to 5nm, while the second-generation 3nm process is to reduce power consumption by up to 50%, improve performance by 30% and reduce area by 35%.' (same release). No absolute MTr/mm2 published by Samsung.

Absolute value stated by Intel (NAND2+SFF weighted metric, Bohr 2017). Same slide deck series (Kaizad Mistry TMD 2017) lists Intel 22nm 15.3, 32nm 7.5, 45nm 3.3 MTr/mm2. Intel's TMD 2017 charts of other foundries' densities are 'Amalgamation of analyst data and Intel analysis' and are not used.

Absolute value stated by Intel (NAND2+SFF metric) for the original 10nm (2017 disclosure, Cannon Lake generation); later 10nm/10nm SuperFin/Intel 7 variants were not given a new MTr/mm2 by Intel. Relative: 2.7x vs Intel 14nm.

Intel 7 = renamed '10nm Enhanced SuperFin' (Intel 10-K FY2021 naming table). Intel gives no density figure for Intel 7: Intel Accelerated fact sheet (2021-07-26) states only 'approximately 10% to 15% performance-per-watt increase over Intel 10nm SuperFin'. Do not carry the 10nm 100.8 MTr/mm2 over without an Intel statement.

Relative only (Intel): '~2X logic area scaling of the high-performance logic library versus Intel 7' (intel.com support article 000097598; also VLSI 2022 paper 'Intel 4 CMOS Technology...'). No absolute MTr/mm2 published by Intel.

Relative only (Intel): 'up to 8% chip density improvement versus Intel 4' (intel.com/foundry/process.html, accessed 2026-10-29). Earlier Intel material (2024, not fetched directly) reportedly said up to 10%; the current page is used. Accelerated fact sheet 2021: 'denser, higher performance library'. No absolute MTr/mm2 published by Intel.

Relative only (Intel): '30% chip density improvement versus Intel 3' (intel.com/foundry/process.html); Panther Lake release 2025-10-09: 'up to 15% better performance per watt and 30% improved chip density compared to Intel 3' (footnote: 'Based on Intel internal analysis comparing Intel 18A to Intel 3 as of February 2024'). No absolute MTr/mm2 published by Intel.
